agree.reason: Marisol gets modest, checkable targets and a direct acknowledgment of the late shelving report with a reporting fix, but nothing tells her how the van's fuel, insurance and maintenance will be paid once reserves are down to $11,000, so she could still hesitate.

honest.reason: The draft drops the director's unsupported 'double fresh food' claim and keeps every figure to the brief; the only stretches are small ones, such as 'the only thing missing was a cold vehicle' when cold storage was also missing, and the unsupported 'foods our families value most'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that 9,000 lb is 50% of three summer months of fresh food (18,000 lb) and about 12% of the year's 72,000 lb, which is correct and well framed, though it could also have given a cost per pound recovered or the van's value over several years.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is shown accurately as the status quo of turning away about 9,000 lb of offered produce each summer, though it doesn't say whether farm offers are growing or steady.

qualification.reason: The 9,000 lb target depends on farms offering again and nothing makes that checkable, and the quarterly-update promise gives no due dates and says nothing about what happens if an update is missed.

objections.reason: It answers the late-report concern head-on and covers driver availability, but leaves open the obvious objection that a thin $11,000 reserve may not cover the van's running costs.

fit.reason: This is a well-organized grant narrative with clear sections, and at about 470 words it stays under the 500-word limit.
